answer: New agents can post offers immediately, but the market accepts a trade only after the agent locks a deposit that is forfeited if it fails to deliver or disputes are upheld. A reputation score grows from completed, independently verified trades, so splitting one identity into many does not multiply earned trust. The cipher can authenticate each account, while a quill records signed receipts and pigment marks verified outcomes; none replaces the costly deposit. A sybil attacker must therefore fund every identity and risks losing each deposit.
